subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Using the BIDMAS order of operations, which operation should always be carried out first?
questions.explain: In BIDMAS the letters stand for Brackets, Indices, Division/Multiplication, then Addition/Subtraction, so brackets come first.

questions.q: Which statement correctly defines a prime number?
options: A number with exactly two factors: 1 and itself
Any number that is divisible by 2
A number with an odd number of factors
questions.explain: A prime number has precisely two distinct factors, one and the number itself.

questions.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 36?
questions.explain: The largest number dividing exactly into both 24 and 36 is 12.

questions.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 8?
questions.explain: 24 is the smallest number that is a multiple of both 6 and 8.

questions.q: Write 0.00056 in standard form.
questions.explain: The digit 5 is in the fourth place after the decimal point, giving 5.6 × 10⁻⁴.

questions.q: What is the value of 7⁰?
questions.explain: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1.

questions.q: Simplify the surd √50.
What is the reciprocal of 4?
questions.explain: The reciprocal of a number n is 1/n, so the reciprocal of 4 is 1/4.

questions.q: Evaluate 2 + 3 × (4 − 1)².
questions.explain: Brackets give 3, squared is 9, then 3 × 9 = 27, and 2 + 27 = 29.

questions.q: What is the value of 3⁻²?
questions.explain: A negative index means the reciprocal, so 3⁻² = 1/3² = 1/9.

questions.q: What is 3/4 written as a percentage?
questions.explain: 3/4 = 0.75, which is equivalent to 75%.

questions.q: Write 0.25 as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.explain: 0.25 = 25/100, which simplifies to 1/4.

questions.q: Calculate 2/3 + 1/6.
questions.explain: Using a common denominator of 6, 2/3 = 4/6, and 4/6 + 1/6 = 5/6.

questions.q: Increase £40 by 25%.
A jacket costs £72 after a 20% reduction. What was its original price?
questions.explain: The sale price is 80% of the original, so the original is £72 ÷ 0.8 = £90.

questions.q: Which of these values is the largest?
questions.explain: Converting all to decimals gives 0.62, 0.6, 0.6 and 0.59, so 62% is greatest.

questions.q: What is 1/3 written as a decimal?
questions.explain: 1 ÷ 3 gives a recurring decimal, 0.333… written as 0.3 with a dot over the 3.

questions.q: Round 3.4567 to 2 decimal places.
questions.explain: The third decimal digit is 6, so the second decimal place rounds up from 5 to 6.

questions.q: Round 45 678 to 3 significant figures.
questions.explain: The first three significant figures are 4, 5, 6; the next digit 7 rounds the 6 up to 7, giving 45 700.

questions.q: A length is measured as 12 cm to the nearest centimetre. What is its error interval?
questions.explain: Rounding to the nearest cm means the true value lies within 0.5 cm, so 11.5 ≤ x < 12.5.
